      <title>The King Who Fled in Sugarcane: Deva Raya II and the Edge of Extinction</title>
      <description>In this chapter, Deva Raya II transforms the Vijayanagara Empire through bitter experience and radical reform. After a shocking battlefield assassination turns the tide against Sultan Firuz, the new Bahmani Sultan Ahmad Shah launches a devastating invasion that catches Deva Raya sleeping in a garden, forcing him to flee disguised as a laborer carrying sugarcane. Ahmad's genocidal rampage provokes a desperate Hindu suicide squad of five thousand warriors who nearly kill the sultan in a mud cattle pen, but the king is ultimately forced into humiliating surrender, sending his own son with treasure-laden elephants to kneel at the sultan's feet. Years later, Deva Raya asks the revolutionary question of why his larger, richer empire keeps losing — and the answer leads him to recruit Muslims into Hindu service, build a mosque in Vijayanagara, and place a Quran before his own throne, creating a reformed military machine that would preserve the empire for generations. Based on A Forgotten Empire (Vijayanagara) by Robert Sewell (1900).</description>
